findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the EC2 user_data script, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with access to the instance metadata, console, or Terraform state.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.

The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with unrestricted egress, which combined with public subnet placement and public IP assignment maximizes the instance's exposed attack surface.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data stored on the volume is unencrypted at rest, risking exposure if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are shared.
The snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, meaning the snapshot data (and any copies/shares made from it) remains unencrypted at rest.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing direct internet exposure of workloads such as web_host.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to any instance launched in this subnet, expanding the network's public attack surface.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to sensitive network traffic metadata.
